arguments.content:
CXX       := clang++
CXXFLAGS  := -std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Iinclude
LDFLAGS   :=

TARGET    := epilog
BUILD_DIR := build
TEST_DIR  := tests

# ---- Source lists ----------------------------------------------------------

SRCS_INTERNALS := $(wildcard internals/*.cpp)
SRCS_PARSER    := $(wildcard parser/*.cpp)
SRCS_ENGINE    := $(wildcard engine/*.cpp)
SRCS_ROOT      := main.cpp repl.cpp

OBJS_INTERNALS := $(patsubst internals/%.cpp, $(BUILD_DIR)/internals/%.o, $(SRCS_INTERNALS))
OBJS_PARSER    := $(patsubst parser/%.cpp,    $(BUILD_DIR)/parser/%.o,    $(SRCS_PARSER))
OBJS_ENGINE    := $(patsubst engine/%.cpp,    $(BUILD_DIR)/engine/%.o,    $(SRCS_ENGINE))
OBJS_ROOT      := $(patsubst %.cpp,           $(BUILD_DIR)/%.o,            $(SRCS_ROOT))

# Shared object files (everything except main.o) linked into each test binary
# epilog_ffi.cpp is included here so FFI tests can be written if desired.
LIB_OBJS := $(OBJS_INTERNALS) $(OBJS_PARSER) $(OBJS_ENGINE) \
            $(BUILD_DIR)/repl.o

TEST_SRCS := $(wildcard $(TEST_DIR)/test_*.cpp)
TEST_BINS := $(patsubst $(TEST_DIR)/%.cpp, $(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%, $(TEST_SRCS))

ALL_OBJS := $(OBJS_INTERNALS) $(OBJS_PARSER) $(OBJS_ENGINE) $(OBJS_ROOT)

# ---- Shared library (for FFI consumers: C, Python, Odin, …) ---------------
#
#   make shared       → build/libepilог.so   (Linux/macOS)
#   make shared_win   → build/epilog.dll     (Windows via clang-cl or MinGW)
#
# The shared lib exposes only epilog_ffi.h symbols.  The engine objects and
# internal headers are not part of the public ABI.

SHARED_OBJS := $(OBJS_INTERNALS) $(OBJS_PARSER) $(OBJS_ENGINE)

LIB_NAME_SO  := $(BUILD_DIR)/libepilог.so
LIB_NAME_DLL := $(BUILD_DIR)/epilog.dll

# ---- Phony targets ---------------------------------------------------------

.PHONY: all release debug clean test coverage shared shared_win

all: release

release: CXXFLAGS += -O2 -DNDEBUG
release: $(TARGET)

debug: CXXFLAGS += -g -O0 -DDEBUG
debug: $(TARGET)

# ---- Main binary -----------------------------------------------------------

$(TARGET): $(ALL_OBJS)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $^ -o $@ $(LDFLAGS)

# ---- Shared library (Linux / macOS) ----------------------------------------

shared: CXXFLAGS += -O2 -DNDEBUG -fPIC
shared: $(SHARED_OBJS)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -shared $^ -o $(LIB_NAME_SO) $(LDFLAGS)
	@echo "Built $(LIB_NAME_SO)"

# ---- Shared library (Windows DLL) -----------------------------------------
#
#   Requires clang++ with lld-link or a MinGW toolchain.
#   Exports are controlled by epilog_ffi.h (all extern "C" symbols).

shared_win: CXXFLAGS += -O2 -DNDEBUG
shared_win: $(SHARED_OBJS)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -shared \
	    -Wl,/DEF:epilog_ffi.def \
	    $^ -o $(LIB_NAME_DLL) $(LDFLAGS)
	@echo "Built $(LIB_NAME_DLL)"

# ---- Tests -----------------------------------------------------------------

test: CXXFLAGS += -g -O0
test: $(LIB_OBJS) $(TEST_BINS)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Running tests ==="
	@PASS=0; FAIL=0; \
	for bin in $(TEST_BINS); do \
	    echo "--- $$bin ---"; \
	    if $$bin; then PASS=$$((PASS+1)); else FAIL=$$((FAIL+1)); fi; \
	done; \
	echo ""; \
	echo "=== $$PASS suite(s) passed, $$FAIL suite(s) failed ==="; \
	[ $$FAIL -eq 0 ]

# ---- Coverage --------------------------------------------------------------

coverage: CXXFLAGS += -g -O0 --coverage -fprofile-arcs -ftest-coverage
coverage: LDFLAGS  += --coverage
coverage: $(LIB_OBJS) $(TEST_BINS)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Running tests for coverage ==="
	@for bin in $(TEST_BINS); do $$bin || true; done
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Generating coverage report ==="
	llvm-cov gcov $(SRCS_INTERNALS) $(SRCS_PARSER) $(SRCS_ENGINE) \
	    --object-directory=$(BUILD_DIR) 2>/dev/null || true
	@echo "Coverage .gcov files written to current directory."

# ---- Compile rules ---------------------------------------------------------

$(BUILD_DIR)/internals/%.o: internals/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/parser/%.o: parser/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/engine/%.o: engine/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: %.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/tests/%: $(TEST_DIR)/%.cpp $(LIB_OBJS)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -I$(TEST_DIR) $^ -o $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR) $(TARGET) $(TARGET).exe *.gcov *.gcda *.gcno \
	       $(LIB_NAME_SO) $(LIB_NAME_DLL)

178

180	The codebase was originally C11 and converted to C++23. Benefits: `constexpr` constants instead of `#define`, `nullptr` instead of `NULL`, `static_cast` instead of C casts, scoped enums, aggregate initialisation, and `bool` instead of `int` for predicate returns. The JPL safety constraints (no post-init heap, bounded loops, no C-stack recursion) are retained.
181	
182	**No heap allocation after init.**
183	Every subsystem uses a fixed-size arena or table declared at startup. `new`/`malloc` are never called during query execution. This follows JPL Rule 3 and makes memory behaviour fully predictable.
184	
185	**No C-stack recursion in the engine.**
186	The unifier uses an explicit `UnifyPair` work stack. The solver uses an explicit `GoalStack` and `ChoiceStack`. `rename_term` recurses only over compound arity (bounded by `TERM_MAX_ARITY = 255`). This follows JPL Rule 1.
187	
188	**Separate arenas for clauses and queries.**
189	Clause terms (asserted facts and rules) live in a persistent `clause_arena`. Each query gets its own `query_arena` that is reset between queries. Stored `TermRef` indices into `clause_arena` remain stable across queries.

191	**Variable names stored in Term nodes.**
192	Each `TERM_KIND_VAR` node carries its source-level name (`char name[64]`). The solver reads names directly from clause-arena term nodes when creating fresh renamed variables for each clause application — no dependency on a stale variable registry.
193	
194	**`TermRef` bindings via `TERM_TERMREF` tag.**
195	Variables are bound to `TermRef` indices (into the query arena) rather than splitting into atom-bindings and var-bindings. This lets `deref` follow any binding — atom, integer, or compound — through a single uniform path.

# Epilog — Implementation Plan

## Phase 0.1: Minimal Prolog Runtime ✅

The foundation. Everything else depends on this being correct.

### Goals
- Parse and store facts and rules
- Unification
- Backtracking search
- Query execution with result enumeration

### Tasks

- [x] Define internal data structures
  - Term representation: atoms, variables, compound terms
  - Clause: head + body
  - Database: ordered list of clauses per functor/arity

- [x] Parser
  - Tokenizer (atoms, variables, numbers, operators, punctuation)
  - Term parser (prefix, infix, parentheses)
  - Clause parser (`head :- body.` and `fact.`)
  - Query parser (`?- goal.`)

- [x] Unification
  - Robinson unification algorithm
  - Occurs check (optional, off by default as in standard Prolog)
  - Substitution (binding environment)

- [x] Execution engine
  - Resolution: match query goal against clause heads
  - Backtracking: undo bindings on failure, try next clause
  - Conjunction: execute body goals left to right
  - Depth-first search (standard Prolog order)

- [x] Built-in predicates (minimal set)
  - `true/0`, `fail/0`, `!/0` (cut)
  - `=/2` (unification), `\=/2` (non-unification)
  - `write/1`, `nl/0`
  - `assert/1`, `retract/1`

- [x] REPL
  - Load a `.pl` file
  - Accept queries interactively
  - Print solutions, prompt for more (`;`)

### Acceptance Criteria ✅

```prolog
parent(alice, bob).
parent(bob, carol).

grandparent(X, Y) :-
    parent(X, Z),
    parent(Z, Y).

?- grandparent(alice, carol).
% true
```

---

## Phase 0.2: Indexing and Caching ✅

Speed up the baseline engine before adding new features.

### Goals
- Reduce clause-scan cost for large fact bases
- Collect query statistics as groundwork for 0.6
- Memoization cache for pure subgoals

### Tasks

- [x] First-argument indexing
  - Hash clauses by the functor/value of the first argument
  - Skip non-matching clauses without trying unification
  - Two-pass bucket build handles interleaved first-arg values correctly
  - Variable first-arg clauses go into a catch-all bucket, always tried
  - Index rebuilt automatically after `assert`; invalidated on `retract`

- [x] Fact indexing
  - Separate fast path for ground fact lookup vs. rule resolution
  - Integer first-args indexed independently from atoms
  - `db_index_range` merges ground bucket + var catch-all in clause order

- [x] Query statistics collector (`include/stats.hpp`, `engine/stats.cpp`)
  - Track which queries are asked and how often (`call_count`)
  - Track total solutions produced per predicate (`soln_count`)
  - `stats_top_n` for identifying hot predicates
  - Wired into FFI layer; reset via `stats_reset`

- [x] Memoization cache / tabling (`include/memo.hpp`, `engine/memo.cpp`)
  - Cache complete solution sets for ground queries
  - `memo_key_from_goal` extracts a ground key (atom + integer args only)
  - Invalidate entire cache on `assert`/`retract` (correctness invariant)
  - Hit/miss counters for observability

- [x] C FFI layer (`include/epilog_ffi.h`, `engine/epilog_ffi.cpp`)
  - Pure C header — usable from C, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, Zig, etc.
  - `epilog_create` / `epilog_destroy` — opaque engine handle
  - `epilog_load_string` — parse and assert clauses from source
  - `epilog_query` + `EpilogCallback` — enumerate solutions
  - Solution inspection: `epilog_soln_var_*` family
  - Stats access: `epilog_stats_call_count`, `epilog_stats_soln_count`
  - `epilog_version_string` — returns `"0.2.0"`

- [x] Shared library build target (`make shared` / `make shared_win`)

### Implementation Notes

**Index correctness bug (fixed):** The initial single-pass bucket build assumed
clauses for the same first-arg value would be contiguous in the clause array.
In practice they can be interleaved (e.g., `f(a). f(b). f(a).`). Fixed with a
two-pass approach: pass 1 classifies each clause into a per-bucket accumulator;
pass 2 lays the buckets out contiguously in `idx_clause_slots[]`.

**Stack size:** `ChoiceStack` and `GoalStack` in the solver are now `static`
locals to stay off the call stack (Windows default 1 MB). Solver remains
non-reentrant by design.

---

## Phase 0.3: Reactive Reasoning (Dependency Graph)

Incremental recomputation when facts change.

### Goals
- Track which conclusions depend on which facts/rules
- On fact change, recompute only affected nodes

### Tasks

- [ ] Dependency graph data structure
  - Node per derived conclusion
  - Directed edges: conclusion → supporting facts/rules
  - Reverse index: fact → conclusions that depend on it

- [ ] Change propagation
  - On `assert`/`retract`, mark dependent conclusions dirty
  - Lazy recomputation: recompute on next query
  - Eager option: recompute immediately (configurable)

- [ ] Diff engine
  - Compute added/removed solutions between old and new state
  - Expose change events for external consumers

### Research Note
This is the "Reasoning DOM" concept — treat the inference graph like a virtual DOM where only dirty subtrees re-render.

---

## Phase 0.4: Database Integration

Make the fact store persistent and scalable.

### Goals
- SQLite-backed fact storage
- Transparent hybrid: some facts in memory, some in DB

### Tasks

- [ ] Storage abstraction layer
  - Interface: `assert_fact`, `retract_fact`, `query_facts`
  - In-memory implementation (existing)
  - SQLite implementation

- [ ] SQLite connector
  - Map Prolog terms to SQL rows
  - Serialize/deserialize compound terms
  - Transactional assert/retract

- [ ] Hybrid fact store
  - Policy: which predicates go to DB vs. memory
  - Cache hot DB facts in memory with invalidation

- [ ] Query planner
  - Push ground arguments down to SQL WHERE clauses
  - Avoid loading full tables for selective queries

---

## Phase 0.5: Graph Reasoning

Native graph traversal as an inference primitive.

### Goals
- Neo4j integration
- Relationship traversal as first-class operations

### Tasks

- [ ] Graph backend interface
  - `node/2`, `edge/3` predicates backed by Neo4j
  - Cypher query generation from Prolog goals

- [ ] Graph-accelerated path finding
  - `path/3`, `reachable/2` using graph indexes
  - Compare performance vs. pure Prolog recursion

- [ ] Use case validation
  - Genealogy queries (grandparent chains)
  - Social network reachability
  - Fraud ring detection (cycle detection)

---

## Phase 0.6: Predictive Execution

Precompute likely future queries on idle cores.

### Goals
- Learn query patterns from statistics (0.2)
- Speculatively compute and cache results before they are requested

### Tasks

- [ ] Pattern learner
  - Identify query sequences that co-occur frequently
  - Build a Markov chain or simple frequency table

- [ ] Speculative executor
  - On query A completion, schedule likely query B on an idle core
  - Store result in speculative cache with TTL

- [ ] Cache management
  - On actual query B arrival: serve from cache, record hit
  - On TTL expiry or cache pressure: discard silently
  - Never serve stale speculative results for non-pure predicates

### Invariant
Speculative results must never be returned if the fact base changed between speculation and query arrival.

---

## Phase 0.7: Multicore Reasoning

Exploit all available CPU cores during inference.

### Goals
- Parallel branch exploration in backtracking search
- Concurrent graph traversal
- Parallel rule evaluation for independent subgoals

### Tasks

- [ ] Work-stealing scheduler
  - Split choice points across worker threads
  - Merge result streams in program order

- [ ] Parallel conjunction
  - Detect independent body goals (no shared variables)
  - Execute them concurrently, join results

- [ ] Concurrency safety
  - Immutable substitution environments (share-nothing)
  - Lock-free fact store reads; serialized writes

---

## Phase 1.0: Stable Release

Harden everything built in 0.1–0.7.

### Tasks

- [ ] Full test suite (unit + integration + conformance)
- [ ] Prolog compatibility suite (standard predicates)
- [ ] Documentation: language reference, architecture guide
- [ ] Performance benchmarks vs. SWI-Prolog
- [ ] Public API stabilization

---

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

These apply across all phases:

- **Correctness over speed**: never let an optimization change a logical result
- **Layered architecture**: inference core has no dependency on prediction or cache layers
- **Testability**: each layer must be testable in isolation
- **Observability**: query stats, cache hit rates, and dependency graph size should be inspectable at runtime

```
│   ├── test_solver.cpp     Phase 0.1 integration tests
│   ├── test_indexing.cpp   Phase 0.2 — first-arg index tests
│   ├── test_stats.cpp      Phase 0.2 — statistics tests
│   └── test_memo.cpp       Phase 0.2 — memoization tests
│
├── repl.cpp              Interactive REPL, file loader
└── main.cpp              Entry point, CLI argument handling
```

### Key Design Decisions

**C++23, not C.**
The codebase was originally C11 and converted to C++23. Benefits: `constexpr`
constants instead of `#define`, `nullptr` instead of `NULL`, `static_cast`
instead of C casts, scoped enums, aggregate initialisation, and `bool` instead
of `int` for predicate returns. The JPL safety constraints (no post-init heap,
bounded loops, no C-stack recursion) are retained.

**No heap allocation after init.**
Every subsystem uses a fixed-size arena or table declared at startup.
`new`/`malloc` are never called during query execution. This follows JPL Rule 3
and makes memory behaviour fully predictable.

**No C-stack recursion in the engine.**
The unifier uses an explicit `UnifyPair` work stack. The solver uses an explicit
`GoalStack` and `ChoiceStack`. `rename_term` recurses only over compound arity
(bounded by `TERM_MAX_ARITY = 255`). This follows JPL Rule 1.

**First-argument indexing (v0.2).**
Each predicate maintains a hash from first-arg value (atom or integer) to a
contiguous list of matching clause positions. Ground queries skip non-matching
clauses entirely. Variable first-arg clauses are always tried via a catch-all
bucket. The index uses a two-pass build to handle interleaved first-arg values
correctly. It is rebuilt after `assert` and invalidated on `retract`.

**Separate arenas for clauses and queries.**
Clause terms (asserted facts and rules) live in a persistent `clause_arena`.
Each query gets its own `query_arena` that is reset between queries. Stored
`TermRef` indices into `clause_arena` remain stable across queries.

**Variable names stored in Term nodes.**
Each `TERM_KIND_VAR` node carries its source-level name (`char name[64]`). The
solver reads names directly from clause-arena term nodes when creating fresh
renamed variables for each clause application — no dependency on a stale
variable registry.

**`TermRef` bindings via `TERM_TERMREF` tag.**
Variables are bound to `TermRef` indices (into the query arena) rather than
splitting into atom-bindings and var-bindings. This lets `deref` follow any
binding — atom, integer, or compound — through a single uniform path.

---

## JPL Coding Standard Compliance

All source files follow the [NASA/JPL Institutional Coding Standard](https://yurichev.com/mirrors/C/JPL_Coding_Standard_C.pdf):

| Rule | How it is applied |
|------|------------------|
| **1** — No recursion | Engine uses explicit `GoalStack`/`ChoiceStack`; unifier uses a `UnifyPair` work stack |
| **2** — Fixed loop bounds | Every loop is bounded by a named `constexpr` capacity constant |
| **3** — No post-init dynamic allocation | All storage is pre-declared in fixed-size structs; no `new`/`malloc` during inference |
| **4** — Short functions | No function exceeds ~60 lines |
| **5** — Check all parameters and return values | Every public function validates inputs; callers check return codes |
| **6** — Preprocessor for includes and constants only | All constants are `constexpr`; no token pasting |
| **7** — Pointer depth ≤ 1 | No `**` in public APIs; all access through flat index types (`TermRef`, `VarId`, `AtomId`) |
| **8** — All warnings enabled | Built with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic` |

---

## Roadmap

| Version | Goal | Status |
|---------|------|--------|
| **0.1** | Minimal Prolog runtime — facts, rules, unification, backtracking, REPL | ✅ Done |
| **0.2** | Indexing and caching — first-arg index, query stats, memo cache, C FFI | ✅ Done |
| 0.3 | Reactive reasoning — dependency graph, incremental recomputation | Planned |
| 0.4 | Database integration — SQLite-backed persistent facts | Planned |
| 0.5 | Graph reasoning — Neo4j integration, relationship traversal | Planned |
| 0.6 | Predictive execution — speculative cache, query pattern learning | Planned |
| 0.7 | Multicore reasoning — parallel branch exploration | Planned |
| 1.0 | Stable release | Planned |

See [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for the detailed task breakdown per phase.

---

## Core Invariant

> Predictions, caching, and speculative execution never alter facts, rules, or logical conclusions.
> The inference engine is always the source of truth.

---

## Name

*Prolog* means "programming in logic."
*Epilog* is what comes after.

Epilog — Changelog
==================

All notable changes are documented here in reverse chronological order.
Format: version / date / summary, then sections Added / Changed / Fixed.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0.2.0 — 2026-06-07
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Phase 0.2: Indexing, Caching, and C FFI.

Added
-----
  engine/database.cpp — First-argument indexing
    * Each predicate of arity >= 1 now maintains a FirstArgIndex.
    * Ground first-arg clauses are partitioned into per-value buckets
      (atom or integer key).  Variable first-arg clauses go into a
      catch-all bucket and are always tried.
    * db_build_index() uses a two-pass algorithm: pass 1 classifies each
      clause; pass 2 lays the buckets out contiguously in idx_clause_slots[].
      This correctly handles interleaved first-arg values (e.g. f(a). f(b).
      f(a).) which a single-pass approach mis-indexed.
    * db_index_range() merges the matching ground bucket with the catch-all
      in ascending clause-position order, preserving Prolog clause ordering.
    * Index is rebuilt automatically after db_assert_last().
    * Index is marked invalid after db_retract_first() (cannot rebuild
      without the TermArena pointer at that call site).

  include/stats.hpp + engine/stats.cpp — Query statistics collector
    * QueryStats tracks call_count and soln_count per (functor, arity).
    * stats_record_call() / stats_record_solutions() — increment counters.
    * stats_get() — point lookup.
    * stats_top_n() — return the N most-called predicates (descending).
    * stats_reset() — zero all counters without removing entries.
    * Designed as groundwork for the Phase 0.6 predictive executor.

  include/memo.hpp + engine/memo.cpp — Memoization (tabling) cache
    * Caches the complete solution set for ground queries (atom + integer
      arguments only; compound arguments and unbound variables are not cached).
    * MemoKey identifies a query by functor, arity, and argument values.
    * memo_begin() / memo_add_solution() / memo_complete() — populate an entry.
    * memo_lookup() — return a complete cached entry; increments hit counter.
    * memo_invalidate() — discard all entries (must be called on assert/retract
      to maintain the correctness invariant).

  include/epilog_ffi.h + engine/epilog_ffi.cpp — C-linkage public API
    * Pure C header (C99+).  No C++ types are exposed.
    * Usable from: C, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, Zig, Rust (FFI), etc.
    * EpilogEngine — opaque handle; one instance = one independent runtime.
    * epilog_create() / epilog_destroy() — lifecycle.
    * epilog_load_string(engine, src) — parse and assert Prolog clauses.
    * epilog_query(engine, goal, callback, userdata) — run a query and
      enumerate solutions via EpilogCallback.
    * EpilogSolution inspection: epilog_soln_var_count, epilog_soln_var_name,
      epilog_soln_var_kind, epilog_soln_var_atom, epilog_soln_var_int,
      epilog_soln_var_functor, epilog_soln_var_arity.
    * Statistics access: epilog_stats_call_count, epilog_stats_soln_count,
      epilog_stats_reset.
    * epilog_version_string() — returns "0.2.0".
    * Query stats are recorded automatically on every epilog_query() call.

  Makefile — Shared library targets
    * `make shared`     — builds build/libepilоg.so   (Linux / macOS, -fPIC)
    * `make shared_win` — builds build/epilog.dll     (Windows)

  tests/test_indexing.cpp — 13 tests covering:
    * Bucket classification for ground atom, ground integer, and variable
      first-arg clauses.
    * db_index_range output for ground queries, unknown-key queries, and
      variable queries.
    * Arity-0 predicate fall-through (no index applied).
    * Solver integration: ground queries return the correct single solution;
      absent-key queries return 0; variable queries return all solutions.
    * Mixed var/ground clauses (f(X):-true. + f(a).) resolved correctly.
    * 10-fact stress: single matching clause returned for ground key.
    * Index rebuild after assert.
    * Phase 0.1 acceptance criteria re-verified with indexing enabled.
    * Integer first-arg indexed independently from atoms.

  tests/test_stats.cpp — 10 tests covering:
    * init / record_call / record_solutions / get / reset.
    * Different arity = different entry.
    * top_n returns entries in descending call_count order.
    * Null-guard and ATOM_ID_INVALID guard.

  tests/test_memo.cpp — 11 tests covering:
    * init / key_from_goal (atom-0 and compound) / begin / lookup /
      add_solution / complete / invalidate / miss counter.
    * key_from_goal returns false for unbound variable arguments.
    * lookup returns nullptr before entry is marked complete.
    * Null-guard.

Changed
-------
  engine/solver.cpp
    * ChoicePoint now stores an explicit candidate list populated by
      db_index_range() rather than a contiguous pred->first..end range.
      This lets the first-argument index prune candidates at choice-point
      creation time.
    * GoalStack, ChoiceStack, and RenameMap in solve() are now `static`
      locals to keep them out of the call stack (Windows default 1 MB limit).
    * Backtrack loop rewritten: a single `while (cs.top > 0)` loop replaces
      the previous goto-based double-backtrack structure.  Each iteration
      restores the trail to cp->trail_mark, tries the next candidate, and
      pops the choice point only after the last candidate succeeds or the
      loop exhausts all candidates.

  include/database.hpp
    * PredEntry now embeds a FirstArgIndex (approx. 2 KB).
    * Added: FirstArgIndex struct, INDEX_MAX_BUCKETS, INDEX_MAX_INDEXED,
      INDEX_MAX_VAR_CLAUSES, IndexKeyKind, IndexKey.
    * New public functions: db_build_index(), db_index_range().

Fixed
-----
  tests/test_atoms.cpp
    * Line 108: `AtomTable t = make_table()` copied a 1 MB struct onto the
      local stack, causing a stack overflow on Windows before any test ran.
      Changed to `AtomTable &t = make_table()` (reference, no copy).
      This was a pre-existing bug first observed during v0.2 testing.

  engine/database.cpp — Index build correctness
    * Single-pass build set bucket->idx_start at the time the bucket was
      first created, then appended slots to a shared flat array as clauses
      were processed in order.  When clauses for the same first-arg value
      were interleaved with clauses for other values, the slot array was not
      contiguous per bucket, causing db_index_range to return wrong clauses.
      Fixed with the two-pass approach described above.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0.1.0 — 2026-06-06
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Phase 0.1: Minimal Prolog Runtime.

Added
-----
  Core data structures
    * AtomTable — FNV-1a open-addressing hash table; O(1) intern/lookup.
    * VarRegistry — per-query logic variable store with Trail undo support.
    * TermArena — fixed-size arena for Term nodes; no malloc after init.
    * ArgPool — flat pool of TermRef[] for compound-term arguments.

  Parser
    * Lexer — single-pass tokenizer (atoms, variables, integers, operators).
    * Parser — iterative top-down parser; handles facts, rules, queries.
      No C-stack recursion.

  Inference engine
    * Unifier — iterative Robinson unification with explicit UnifyPair work
      stack.  Trail records all variable bindings; trail_undo() restores state.
    * Database — predicate-indexed clause store; db_assert_last / db_retract_first.
    * Solver — backtracking SLD resolution using GoalStack + ChoiceStack.
      No C-stack recursion.  Clause variables are renamed (fresh VarIds) on
      each application.

  Built-in predicates
    * true/0, fail/0, false/0
    * !/0 (cut — clears entire choice stack)
    * =/2 (unification), \=/2 (non-unification)
    * write/1, nl/0
    * assert/1, assertz/1, retract/1

  REPL
    * Interactive query loop with solution printing and `;` prompting.
    * `consult('file.pl')` loads a file at runtime.
    * `halt.` exits.
